headline: Tk 500cr embezzlement: Islami Bank files ACC complaint against S Alam and others
summary: The bank alleges that loan limits for Suprov Composite Knit Ltd were illegally increased from Tk 100 crore to Tk 500 crore, leading to the embezzlement of funds.
details: Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC has filed a formal complaint with the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) against 38 people, including S Alam Group Chairman Saiful Alam and former bank president Mohammed Shahabuddin.
The complaint alleges the embezzlement of approximately Tk 500 crore through irregularities in the loan process for Suprov Composite Knit Ltd, an associate company of AnnonTex Group.
According to the bank, the loan limit for Suprov Composite Knit Ltd was illegally increased from Tk 100 crore to Tk 500 crore after S Alam Group took control of the bank in 2017.
The bank alleges that Mohammed Shahabuddin, while serving as vice-chairman and a board member, along with three former managing directors, played key roles in approving the loan.
Four audit firms were appointed to investigate the incident, and their findings revealed various irregularities in the increasing of the loan limit, approval, and disbursement of funds.

The bank has requested the ACC to investigate whether the money was used in a manner detrimental to theB ank's interests and whether the individuals involved financially benefited from the irregularities.
caption:
Tk 500 crore embezzled? Islami Bank has filed an ACC complaint against S Alam Group Chairman and 37 others.

Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC has filed a formal complaint with the Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) against 38 people, including S Alam Group Chairman Saiful Alam and former bank president Mohammed Shahabuddin.

The complaint alleges the embezzlement of approximately Tk 500 crore through irregularities in the loan process for Suprov Composite Knit Ltd, an associate company of AnnonTex Group.

According to the bank, the loan limit for Suprov Composite Knit Ltd was illegally increased from Tk 100 crore to Tk 500 crore after S Alam Group took control of the bank in 2017.

The bank alleges that Mohammed Shahabuddin, while serving as vice-chairman and a board member, along with three former managing directors, played key roles in approving the loan.

Four audit firms were appointed to investigate the incident, and their findings revealed various irregularities in the increasing of the loan limit, approval, and disbursement of funds.

The bank has requested the ACC to investigate whether the money was used in a manner detrimental to theB ank's interests and whether the individuals involved financially benefited from the irregularities.

headline_marked: Measles outbreak: [[5 children die in 24 hours]] as toll rises
headline: Measles outbreak: 5 children die in 24 hours as toll rises
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services reports that 1,155 children were infected with measles or measles-like symptoms in a single day.
details: Five children died within 24 hours due to measles symptoms, according to a report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) on Monday.
During the same period, 1,155 children were infected with measles or showed symptoms of the disease.
The DGHS clarified that while these children died with measles symptoms, none of the deaths have been confirmed as measles through laboratory testing.
Since March 15, a total of 780 children have died nationwide showing symptoms of measles.
The trend follows a similar pattern from Sunday, August 9, when six children died and 1,063 children were infected with measles or measles-like symptoms.
